summary: Complete catalogue-wide screen of tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves (13 layers, read in full) against all 211 other atlas roadmaps and the new roadmap MordellLawrenceVenkatesh. Each partner was screened by summary, stage titles and a keyword search of stage descriptions and documents. Every candidate stage pair was decided by reading both descriptions in full. Result: 50 links and 11 overlaps; 17 roadmaps have links or overlaps and 195 have none. Outgoing links (44; 4 inferred, the rest explicit) supply function-field places, divisors, L(D), genus, Riemann–Roch consequences, extension ramification, the different and Hurwitz, constant-field extension and ramification groups, Kähler/Weil differentials and the curve/function-field dictionary. Their consumers are BelyiMaps Layers 9–12 (18 links), EllipticCurves Layer 0 (4), ModularCurves Layer 10 (4), SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.3 (3), K2SymbolsBrauer T.4 (3), FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.4 (3), FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.2/FA.5 (2, inferred), MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.7 (2), and one each for EllipticKTheory E.1, WeilConjectures WC.5, ColemanIntegration L1, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6 and EllipticCurveModularity R29.6. Incoming links (6, all explicit): EllipticCurves Layer 0 → Layer 10 (toClass_surjective); EllipticCurves Layer 1 → Layers 9 and 12 (invariant differential, isogeny type); JacobianChallenge Layers A and B → Layer 12 (comparison contract); LocalFieldsRamification Layer 3 → Layer 8 (upper numbering, Herbrand, Hasse–Arf). Overlaps: nine rescope and two keep. The rescope overlaps are EllipticCurves Layers 0 and 1 (the Weierstrass dictionary; dim Ω = 1), FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.0/FA.1/FA.3 (duplicates Layers 0–12 over finite fields), JacobianChallenge Layer A (Weil divisors), EllipticKTheory E.1 with ModularCurves 2A (Weierstrass isogeny–scheme comparison), LocalFieldsRamification Layer 3 (local different theory) and NumberFieldArithmetic Layers 5–6 (global-to-local transport of the different). Riemann–Roch against JacobianChallenge Layer B and ModularForms 10B is kept. Supplier gaps found: BelyiMaps 10.6/12.4 expect Layer 8 to supply fully faithful base change along ℚ̄ ⊂ ℂ; ColemanIntegration expects de Rham complexes; SchemeKTheoryOperations KU-geometry cites nonexistent AlgebraicCurves vector bundles.

overlaps.detail: Both stages develop the elliptic function-field dictionary for Weierstrass curves. It has three parts: (a) the coordinate ring of an elliptic W is integrally closed and Dedekind, the integral closure of k[x] (AlgebraicCurves 10.ii; EllipticCurves Layer 0's Dedekind lemma, with Layer 1's isIntegrallyClosed_coordinateRing); (b) W.toAffine.Point ≃ degree-1 places, O ↦ infinity place (AlgebraicCurves 10.iii; EllipticCurves Layer 0's point–place dictionary); (c) the class-group/principal-divisor identification (AlgebraicCurves 10.iv with Prop. 6.1.6–6.1.7; EllipticCurves Layer 0's class-group anchor and principal-divisor characterisation). AlgebraicCurves says it supplies (ii) and (iii) to EllipticCurves; EllipticCurves builds them in its foundation layer, on which every later EllipticCurves layer depends. AlgebraicCurves Layer 10 depends on Layers 7 and 9.
overlaps.proposal: Make EllipticCurves Layer 0 the single owner of the Weierstrass-specific dictionary (a)–(c), built on AlgebraicCurves Layers 0, 2 and 3 (recorded links). AlgebraicCurves Layer 10 keeps the intrinsic genus-1 theory: Def. 6.1.1, normal forms, the group law of Prop. 6.1.6–6.1.7 for any elliptic function field, and genus 1 of W.FunctionField (10.i). It states (ii)–(iv) as citations of EllipticCurves Layer 0 instead of second proofs, so the early EllipticCurves foundation no longer waits on a late AlgebraicCurves layer.

overlaps.detail: Both prove that the Kähler differentials of a function field are one-dimensional. AlgebraicCurves Layer 9 proves dim_F Ω[F⁄k] = 1 with basis dx for any separating x, using Layers 0–3 only. EllipticCurves Layer 1 proves Ω[F⁄K] is 1-dimensional over F with basis ω = dx/(2y + a₁x + a₃) for W.FunctionField. Neither link direction fits at stage level: AlgebraicCurves Layer 9's EllipticCurves compatibility milestone already consumes EllipticCurves Layer 1's invariant differential (recorded link), so a link back would make a cycle.
overlaps.proposal: Split AlgebraicCurves Layer 9's first subsection (dim_F Ω[F⁄k] = 1 with basis dx; Layers 0–3 only) into its own stage. EllipticCurves Layer 1 derives 'Ω[F⁄K] has basis ω' from it as the instance at the separating element x, since ω = dx/(2y + a₁x + a₃) with nonzero denominator. The comparison theorem and the compatibility milestone stay in Layer 9 after Layer 7, still consuming the invariant differential.

overlaps.detail: Both prove Riemann–Roch for curves over a field, by different routes. AlgebraicCurves Layer 4 uses repartitions and Weil differentials on the function field: ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g + ℓ(W − D), canonical class, deg W = 2g − 2. JacobianChallenge Layer B uses coherent cohomology: χ(L) = deg L + 1 − g with g = dim H¹(X, 𝒪_X), and Serre duality with deg ω = 2g − 2. Both define a genus and a canonical/dualizing object.
overlaps.proposal: Keep both routes. The function-field route works over arbitrary k with no cohomology, and the Jacobian construction needs the sheaf-theoretic route. AlgebraicCurves 12E is the reconciliation: H⁰ = L(D), dim H¹(X, 𝒪_X) = genus k F, dualizing sheaf = canonical class. Neither roadmap should prove the other's Riemann–Roch.

overlaps.detail: Both define Weil divisors and their degree on a regular proper curve over k. AlgebraicCurves 12A–12D define the closed-point degree and Weil divisors on the regular model X_F, and prove principal divisors, linear equivalence and Pic-style class groups agree with Cl(F). JacobianChallenge Layer A defines Weil divisors ⊕_x ℤ, principal divisors, Cl(X) ≅ Pic X and deg = Σ_x [κ(x):k]·ord_x. The carrier also differs: AlgebraicCurves 12A takes 'curve over k' to mean an integral proper 1-dimensional scheme; JacobianChallenge works with smooth proper geometrically connected curves. AlgebraicCurves assigns the scheme-side divisor namespace to Mathlib, not to itself.
overlaps.proposal: AlgebraicCurves 12D should take its Weil divisor group, degree and Cl(X) ≅ Pic X from JacobianChallenge Layer A, or from Mathlib's AlgebraicCycle when the pin reaches it. It then proves only Weil divisors on X_F ≅ Divisor k F, with degrees and principal divisors matched. The 'curve over k' of 12A should be named as the regular (not necessarily smooth) carrier and related to JacobianChallenge's smooth proper geometrically connected curve by one lemma.

overlaps.detail: Both prove the Riemann–Roch chain for curves: ℓ(D) − ℓ(K − D) = deg D + 1 − g, deg K = 2g − 2, the dimension of regular differentials is g, and residue-theorem lemmas. AlgebraicCurves does it for function fields over arbitrary k (Layers 4–5, with residues in Layer 9). ModularForms Layer 10B does it for compact Riemann surfaces by Čech cohomology and Forster's residue duality. AlgebraicCurves records that ModularForms consumes nothing from it, and ModularForms 10C disclaims the analytic/algebraic comparison.
overlaps.proposal: Keep both. The carriers differ (compact Riemann surfaces vs function fields over arbitrary fields), and GAGA is outside every current roadmap. The only comparison needed so far is at Belyi generality, owned by BelyiMaps 9.5, which consumes both (recorded links from AlgebraicCurves Layers 3, 5, 12).

overlaps.detail: FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.0 builds, for curves over a perfect field and then over F_q, the normalization of a projective model, the contravariant correspondence between one-variable function fields and smooth projective curves, closed points = discrete valuations trivial on constants, and finiteness of the exact constant field. AlgebraicCurves Layer 12 (12A–12C: normalize ℙ¹_k in F, closed points = places, anti-equivalence) and Layer 0 (constant field k̃ finite, F/k̃ exact) build the same objects over an arbitrary field. AlgebraicCurves names a future curves-over-finite-fields roadmap as its consumer, a role FunctionFieldArithmetic fills.
overlaps.proposal: Rescope FA.0 to consume AlgebraicCurves Layer 12's anti-equivalence and point–place dictionary and Layer 0's constant-field results, specialized to finite perfect k. FA.0 keeps only the F_q-specific statements: geometric connectedness from exact constants, and the F_q(t)/F_{q^m}(t) acceptance examples.

overlaps.detail: FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.1 builds effective divisors, residue-degree-weighted degree, the product formula for principal divisors, L(D), canonical divisors, residue maps and finiteness of Pic⁰(F_q), and moves curve Riemann–Roch (from SF.3) to function-field linear algebra. AlgebraicCurves proves the same over arbitrary k: Layer 3 (divisors, degree, product formula, L(D), genus), Layer 4 (canonical class, Riemann–Roch), Layer 5 (Finite Cl⁰(F) over finite k, local components, abstract residue theorem) and Layer 9 (residues, residue theorem). FA.2's global residue pairing is Layer 5's decomposition ω = ∑_P ω_P.
overlaps.proposal: Rescope FA.1 to consume AlgebraicCurves Layers 3–5 and 9 instead of transporting scheme Riemann–Roch. Layer 5's finite-constant-field subsection, including the class number h_F, was written for this consumer. FA.1 keeps the arithmetic-specific content: the distinction between rational divisor classes and rational points, certified bases of L(D), and the no-rational-point acceptance test.

overlaps.detail: FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.3 builds, for finite separable extensions of global function fields, integral closures, decomposition and inertia groups, different and discriminant, lower and upper ramification filtrations, Riemann–Hurwitz with the wild different, Artin–Schreier covers and the separate treatment of purely inseparable extensions. AlgebraicCurves builds the same over arbitrary constant fields: Layer 6 (integral closures, e, f, Galois action), Layer 7 (different, Dedekind's theorem, Hurwitz), Layer 8 (decomposition/inertia/lower ramification groups, Hilbert's formula, inseparable steps) and Layer 10 (Kummer and Artin–Schreier covers with d = (p − 1)(m_P + 1)).
overlaps.proposal: Rescope FA.3 to consume AlgebraicCurves Layers 6–8 and 10's cover calculus, specialized to finite constant fields. It keeps the discriminant, the upper numbering (from LocalFieldsRamification for the finite residue fields of global function fields) and the Witt-vector description of cyclic p-power extensions, which AlgebraicCurves does not build.

overlaps.detail: Three stages develop the comparison of equation-level Weierstrass objects with schemes. AlgebraicCurves 12C obtains, as an acceptance instance of its anti-equivalence, the correspondence between W.FunctionField isogenies and scheme morphisms. EllipticKTheory E.1 rebuilds, over a field, the smooth projective scheme of a Weierstrass equation, identifies its function field, and constructs the same isogeny/scheme-morphism comparison. It claims the elliptic specialisation for itself. ModularCurves 2A proves K(projModel W) ≃ W.toAffine.FunctionField over any base, but only for [N]. It assigns the broad isogeny comparison to AlgebraicCurves, as do ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations and EllipticCurveModularity.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the general anti-equivalence in AlgebraicCurves 12C. Promote the Weierstrass isogeny ↔ scheme-morphism correspondence there from acceptance instance to a named milestone. It should consume ModularCurves 1A/2A's projective model and K(projModel W) ≃ W.toAffine.FunctionField, a compatibility lemma rather than a second construction. EllipticKTheory E.1 then imports ModularCurves 1A/1B/2A for the scheme model and AlgebraicCurves 12C for the comparison, keeping only what neither supplier states: the zero morphism, and the degree, kernel, divisor-pullback and invariant-differential identifications used by its K-theory.

overlaps.detail: Both prove the local theory of the different and the lower ramification filtration. LocalFieldsRamification Layer 3 proves, for local fields: d(L/K) = e − 1 iff L/K is tame, Hilbert's formula d = ∑_{i≥0}(|G_i| − 1) for Galois L/K, and the embeddings G₀/G₁ ↪ residue units (cyclic, prime to p) and G_i/G_{i+1} ↪ residue field (elementary abelian p). AlgebraicCurves Layer 7 builds the exact tame value d = e − 1 by a complete local route for complete DVRs with separable residue extension and arbitrary residue field. Layer 8 proves the same structure of G_i and Hilbert's different formula, plus the completion bridge at arbitrary residue fields. AlgebraicCurves takes only upper numbering, Herbrand and Hasse–Arf from LocalFieldsRamification (recorded link), and only for finite residue fields.
overlaps.proposal: State LocalFieldsRamification Layer 3's different and lower-numbering theorems (tame equality criterion, Hilbert's formula, structure of G_i/G_{i+1}) for complete discretely valued fields with separable residue extension, which is the generality of their proofs in Serre, Local Fields III–IV. Derive the local-field forms as corollaries. AlgebraicCurves Layers 7–8 then consume these at completions of places and keep only the function-field statements (Diff(F′/F), function-field-level G_i, Hurwitz) and the completion bridge.

overlaps.detail: Both carry local ramification data to a global Dedekind extension. NumberFieldArithmetic 5.9 proves the different localizes to completions. Its 6.2 identifies the global ideal-theoretic ramification groups with the local lower filtration, and 6.3–6.4 carry Hilbert's formula and the tame and wild exponents across, restricted to number fields. NumberFieldArithmetic records that a Dedekind-generic transport is missing. For affine models of function fields, AlgebraicCurves Layer 7 proves that localization preserves the trace dual and the different and that completion preserves the different exponent. Layer 8 proves the completion bridge G_i = local G_i.
overlaps.proposal: Prove the transport once, for a finite separable extension of Dedekind domains with fraction fields (AKLB) and a prime with separable residue extension: the different commutes with completion, and the global ramification groups match the local filtration under the decomposition map. NumberFieldArithmetic 5.9/6.2 then specialize it to number fields, and AlgebraicCurves Layers 7–8 to the affine models R_x of a function field.
